author: reek
body: The self-compile cannot catch a regression here: the compiler does no floating-point arithmetic of its own, so no amount of fixed-point green exercises the negation rule on a Real. It went unnoticed that `-(f x)`, where f returns a Real, was typed as an Integer: the inference rule saw that the operand's type was not YET known to be Real -- an application's result is still an unresolved variable at that moment -- and unified it with Integer, which then collided with the declared Real. Negating a Real-returning CALL was rejected while negating a Real variable was fine.

author: reek
body: The casualty was codex/foreword/math/Matrix4.codex, whose mat4-inverse and mat4-look-at negate calls (`-(mat4-at a 0 1)`, `-(vec3-dot right eye)`), which took the whole 3D stack with it -- the engine quire, globe, spark.

author: reek
body: Each of these is a Real. The compiler must not decide any of them is an Integer.

author: reek
body: Negation inside a larger Real expression: the shape Matrix4 actually uses.

author: reek
body: Reals are reported as scaled integers so the expected output does not depend on float formatting.
